summary.text: A 50-year-old woman with an unremarkable medical history and no similar family history presented with worsening exertional breathlessness, paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnea, oliguria and leg edema. At another hospital she was diagnosed with valvular heart disease and heart failure (NYHA Class IV) and started on spironolactone, furosemide and beta-blockers, which she stopped after 2 months, with edema and breathlessness returning before referral to the authors’ outpatient clinic.

Examination showed marked jugular venous distention, moderate hepatomegaly, bilateral leg edema and rales. NT-proBNP was 3,709 pg/ml and high-sensitivity troponin I 351.28 ng/L; ECG showed low limb-lead voltage with a pseudoinfarction pattern, and echocardiography showed a non-dilated left ventricle with normal wall thickness, no granular sparkling echotexture, restrictive filling with grade 3 diastolic dysfunction and mild pericardial effusion.

Symptoms worsened and she was readmitted on 22 March 2022 with NT-proBNP 6,152 pg/ml, elevated free lambda light chains, an abnormally low kappa/lambda ratio, a lambda-lane precipitating band on immunofixation, decreased global longitudinal strain with relative apical sparing, and Congo red-positive extracardiac biopsies. Later cardiac MRI showed delayed gadolinium enhancement, wall thickness increased and granular sparkling echotexture appeared, and bone marrow showed an abnormal plasma cell phenotype, confirming light chain (lambda) cardiac amyloidosis.

She was treated with heart failure drugs plus bortezomib, daratumumab and dexamethasone. One month after starting treatment free lambda light chains had fallen to 31.70 mg/L and NT-proBNP was 2,872 pg/ml at 3 months with heart failure symptoms improved, but she had recurrent heart failure episodes with NYHA class fluctuating between II and IV, and she died of heart failure in July 2023.
